_comment: 3-way cross-binding parity fixtures (issue #1455).
Each fixture names ONE SELECT that is run through all three legs (Python
binding, Node binding, CLI --out json) and canonicalized to the SAME JSON.
`columns` declares the CQL type of every column the query returns. It is
the AUTHORITATIVE input to canonicalization (issue #28: no type guessing
from value shapes), and the harness asserts that the declared column set
equals the set every leg actually returns -- so schema drift reds the test
rather than silently changing what is compared.
`known_divergence` is EMPTY for every fixture and must stay that way. It
exists so a future, deliberately-accepted gap has somewhere to be recorded
with a reason; it is NOT a place to silence a real cross-binding bug. The
issue originally proposed allowlisting `duration` and `time` until #1450
landed -- #1450 IS landed, and all three legs were measured to agree
exactly on both, so nothing is allowlisted.
`sstables_root` (optional, checkout-relative): the SSTables root this fixture reads
INSTEAD of the shared datasets root. Used by `varint_values` (#4360), whose
Cassandra 5.0.8-written table lives under test-data/fixtures/issue_4360 and is
therefore visible whatever CQLITE_DATASETS_ROOT points at.
`floor` (issue #1455, B2) is the case floor: an empty or truncated fixture
list would otherwise produce an EMPTY pytest parametrize — one skipped
placeholder and the 3-way comparison silently gone, green. The floor names
the fixtures by NAME, not just a count, so swapping one for a trivial
substitute is caught too.

fixtures.name: signed_special_decimals
fixtures._why: Issue #4350: a decimal with MORE significant digits than an f64 holds must compare EXACTLY across all three legs. This committed table carries Cassandra-written decimals of 33 significant digits (-999999999999999999999999999999.999 and 123456789012345678901234567890.123), which the CLI emits as UNQUOTED JSON numbers (#3644). A harness that parsed the CLI JSON through a float would see both collapse to ~17 digits. `sf` (set<double>, NaN/Infinity) is deliberately NOT selected: it is outside this fixture's subject.

fixtures.name: varint_values
fixtures._why: Issue #4360: a top-level `varint` column with values beyond 2^64, negatives, sign-byte edges (127/128/-128/-129) and a no-cell NULL, Cassandra 5.0.8-written (test-data/scripts/generate-issue-4360-varint-column.sh). The CLI emits a varint as an UNQUOTED JSON integer (IntegerType.toJSONString), which must compare EXACTLY with the bindings' bigint/int. DECLARED GAP: the fixture's explicit-NULL row (id 100) is dropped by CQLite's SELECT on all three legs alike (a row with only a null cell; class of #2189), so the NULL case is NOT compared here; it is pinned by the ignored cqlite-core test issue_4360_varint_column_oracle::null_varint_row_is_returned_as_null.
